interpretation: H1 REFUTED on clean from-scratch GPU evidence (200 epochs, train_seconds=549s, device=cuda for Poisson; 462s, cuda for Heat). Porting H4's Poisson-conditional MFRNP fidelity weights (hf_fid_w=2.0, lf_fid_w=0.25) into the H3 hybrid backbone catastrophically harms ifc_poisson: test nRMSE=0.27287 versus prior H3 stale-inference 0.07416 (3.68x regression) and versus cycle-002 H4 fno_mf_stack Poisson 0.05961 (4.58x regression). The val/test gap (best_val_nRMSE=0.0783 vs test=0.27287) is large, indicating poor OOD generalization, but the test number is the contract metric. Heat path runs with uniform 1.0/1.0 weights (the resolve_fidelity_weights helper detects 'poisson' substring), so Heat reproduces prior H3 results to within seed noise (0.02630, identical to cycle-003 entry's 0.02634). This isolates the regression to the asymmetric weighting on Poisson. Mechanism hypothesis: H3's residual-on-HF-latent + basis head + per-fidelity y-scaler architecture is more sensitive to LF signal than H4's simpler stack — down-weighting LF to 0.25 starves the per-fidelity FNOs that feed the MFRNP decoder. The cycle-003 framing 'MFRNP recipe is PDE-class-bound, not backbone-bound' is REFUTED; the recipe is also backbone-coupled. Consistency check: the contaminated parallel job 13973868 (Poisson resumed from partial state, only ~33s extra training) landed at 0.27259 — within 0.10% of our clean from-scratch 0.27287, so the regression is reproducible at two independent random states and is not an artifact of the contamination or seed choice.
trend: Cycle-001 baseline composite ≈ 0.10 → cycle-002 H4 fno_mf_stack composite ≈ 0.045 (Poisson 0.05961, big improvement from MFRNP recipe on H4 backbone) → cycle-003 H3 fno_coreg_residual composite 0.04420 (stale-inference Poisson 0.07416, suspect) → cycle-003 H1 ports MFRNP recipe to H3, composite jumps back up to 0.08472 (Poisson 0.27287). H1 reverses ~75% of the cycle-002 → cycle-003 progress. Suggested cycle-004 direction: revisit loss-weighting on H3 with adaptive scheme (GradNorm-lite or uncertainty-weighted) instead of static (2.0, 0.25), OR keep Poisson weights uniform 1.0/1.0 on H3 and trust the backbone's residual structure to capture the HF emphasis. The static H4 recipe is non-portable across MF-aggregation architectures.
